deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is a heavily corrected pencil draft of the opening of a letter, addressed 'Hochgeehrtester Herr Professor!' ('Most highly honoured Professor!').

The writer makes several false starts and strikes each one through:
- 'Es ist mir unmöglich, ... in einer Angelegenheit, die sich auf einen so ausführlichen Aufsatz ...' ('It is impossible for me, ... in a matter that concerns so detailed an essay ...')
- '... ein dringendes Bedürfniß, mich Ihnen gegenüber ...' ('... a pressing need, towards you ...')
- 'Es ist mir ein unabweisliches Bedürfniß / nicht möglich gewesen ...' ('It is an irresistible need for me / it has not been possible ...')

The one surviving (unstruck) opening is: 'Ich kann es nicht unterlassen, auch in einer Angelegenheit, die sie [für?] mich ...' ('I cannot refrain, also in a matter which ... me ...'). The sentence breaks off.

The folio number 134 is in the right margin.

The next page continues the same drafting under 'Hochgeehrter Herr Verfasser!' ('Highly honoured Author!'). There the writer speaks of a matter in which an injustice ('Unrecht') has been done to the addressee, and of wanting to come to clarity about it. That page then names 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen v. B. Riemann' and its 'erste Abtheilung' (first part).

So the draft seems to be a personal letter, perhaps an apology or a statement on a question of credit, to a professor or author whose work touches Riemann's 1857 theory of Abelian functions. Who the addressee is cannot be read from this page. Weierstrass, or an author whose prior work was not acknowledged, are only possibilities; this is unsure. No derivation is present to reconstruct.

results.what: Draft opening of a personal letter (no mathematical content), apparently about a sensitive matter connected with Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen'.

deep.surprise_reason: There is no mathematics on the page. It is only a struck-through letter draft. Its biographical interest depends entirely on identifying the addressee, which this page alone does not allow.
transcription_corrections: In the struck line beginning 'Es ist mir unmöglich ... ein dringendes Bedürfniß', the word before 'eine Angelegenheit' carries a correction mark. It may read 'für' rather than 'in'.
In the surviving sentence, 'die sie mich' may be 'die für mich' or 'die Sie [an]mich'. The reading is uncertain.
In the last struck line, the word read as 'Bedürfniß[?]' after 'unabweisliches' is doubtful from the image. The line reads roughly 'Es ist mir ein unabweisliches ... nicht möglich gewesen'.
'namentlich[?]' in the second line is uncertain. The struck word may instead be 'unmöglich' or similar.
